structured_output.rationale:
Both files rendered issue_codes via .map().reduce((prev, curr) => [prev,
, curr]), producing nested unkeyed element arrays (4 react/jsx-key violations). issue_codes[].code is a stable unique identifier (used by IssueCode to build the docs URL), so the lists were rewritten with flatMap keyed on issueCode.code and `br-${issueCode.code}` for the separators, matching the existing DatabaseErrorMessage pattern in the same directory. No index keys, no lint-disable/ts-ignore, no oxlint.json change, nothing touched outside src/components. Verified: check 1 printed 0; check 2 printed 77; tests 11 passed in 2 suites (the given .tsx paths match no Jest testRegex, so the .test.tsx paths were used); npm run type fails with 68 pre-existing TS6305 errors from unbuilt deckgl plugins (npm run plugins:build fails on a pre-existing TS2352 in preset-chart-deckgl) — identical 68 errors on unmodified master, none referencing src/components. Behavior change: TimeoutErrorMessage previously threw a TypeError when issue_codes was empty (reduce with no initial value); it now renders nothing. Stated explicitly in the PR body.

messages.message:
## Repository

`CognitionTakeHomeOrg/superset-adham-clone`, branched from `master` at `9f5611aca5425416d6eecd9ebe68fa3c865c4abe`.

Superset's own conventions are in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root.
Read them and follow them -- in particular: no `any` types, functional
components, and import UI components from `@superset-ui/core`.

## Task

There are 4 `react/jsx-key` violations in `src/components` (2 files). This rule is
checked on every CI run and enforced on none of them, because `npm run lint`
passes `--quiet`, which hides findings but still counts them.

`superset-frontend/src/components/ErrorMessage/ParameterErrorMessage.tsx`
  line 109, col 14: Missing "key" prop for element in iterator.
  line 110, col 45: Missing "key" prop for element in array.

`superset-frontend/src/components/ErrorMessage/TimeoutErrorMessage.tsx`
  line 66, col 12: Missing "key" prop for element in iterator.
  line 67, col 43: Missing "key" prop for element in array.

## Definition of done

Run these yourself and confirm each one before opening a pull request. All paths
are relative to `superset-frontend/`. Use the lockfile-pinned binary at
`./node_modules/.bin/oxlint`, **not** `npx` -- npx may resolve a different
version than the lockfile and give you a different answer than CI.

```bash
cd superset-frontend

# 1. This area is clean.
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config oxlint.json -A all -D react/jsx-key --format json \
  | jq '[.diagnostics[] | select(.filename | startswith("src/components/"))] | length'
# must print 0

# 2. Nothing else regressed. The repo-wide count for this rule must be exactly
#    77, down from 81. Higher means you broke something; lower means
#    you changed files outside the scope of this task.
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config oxlint.json -A all -D react/jsx-key --format json \
  | jq '.diagnostics | length'

# 3. Types still check.
npm run type

# 4. Tests still pass for what you touched.
npm run test -- src/components/ErrorMessage/ParameterErrorMessage.tsx src/components/ErrorMessage/TimeoutErrorMessage.tsx
```

## Constraints

- **`key={index}` is not an acceptable fix.** Keying by array position is the precise behaviour this rule exists to prevent: when the list is reordered or filtered, React reuses the wrong DOM node and renders stale content against the wrong label. Find a stable unique identifier in the data being mapped and key on that. If no stable identifier exists, say so rather than falling back to the index.
- Fix the cause, not the symptom.
- Do not modify `oxlint.json`, and do not add any lint-disable or `@ts-ignore`
  comment. Changing the rule's configuration is a failed session, not a fix.
- Do not touch files outside `src/components`.
- If a correct fix requires changing runtime behaviour, make the change and state
  it explicitly in the pull request body. Do not hide it.
- **If you cannot fix something correctly, stop and explain why.** A blocked
  session is a valid, expected outcome and a human will review it. A fix that
  passes the linter while preserving the defect is not a valid outcome.

## Pull request

Open a PR against `master` of `CognitionTakeHomeOrg/superset-adham-clone`. Follow `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
and Conventional Commits, e.g. `fix(components): add stable keys to error message lists`.
State in the body which of the four checks above you ran and what they printed.

## Output

Conform to the provided structured output schema. `gate_closed` must be true only
if check 1 actually printed 0 when you ran it.
On it — reading the two ErrorMessage components and finding stable keys.

Fixed and PR opened: https://github.com/CognitionTakeHomeOrg/superset-adham-clone/pull/2

Keyed the `issue_codes` lists on `issueCode.code` (stable unique id) via `flatMap`, matching the existing `DatabaseErrorMessage` pattern; no index keys, no suppressions. Checks: gate 1 printed 0, repo-wide count 77, tests 11 passed. `npm run type` shows 68 pre-existing `TS6305` errors from unbuilt deckgl plugins — identical on unmodified master, none in `src/components`. One behavior change, stated in the PR body: `TimeoutErrorMessage` with empty `issue_codes` previously threw (`reduce` on empty array) and now renders nothing.
